plain_english_policy:
This bill creates a new category of 'part-time reserve school resource officers' (SROs) in Alabama schools. It allows retired police officers and deputy sheriffs who resigned in good standing to work part-time as SROs.

Key policy changes include:
- **Eligibility**: Retired law enforcement certified by the state commission can serve part-time if they resigned in good standing.
- **Certification Waiver**: These reserve officers do not need to meet physical fitness exams or continuing education requirements, except for firearms and use-of-force training.
- **Benefits Limitation**: They are ineligible for new health insurance or retirement benefits beyond what their former employer provided.
- **Immunity**: Chiefs of police/sheriffs get civil liability immunity when acting as reserve SROs.
- **Funding & Pay**: Funding can come from local, state, federal sources; pay is set by the hiring authority without tying to existing scales.

The bill aims to expand school safety staffing using experienced retired officers while reducing certification burdens and costs compared to full-time positions.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would allow schools in Alabama to hire part-time reserve SROs from among qualified retirees, expanding access to law enforcement presence without requiring new physical/education certifications. This could increase school safety staffing flexibility but may reduce overall training standards for these specific roles compared to full-time officers.
sponsorship_supports_position: Representative Ford (Public Safety and Homeland Security) supports expanding part-time reserve SRO programs using retired officers with reduced certification requirements.
evidence_quotes: This bill would allow retired police officers or other law enforcement officers who resigned in good standing to serve on a part-time basis as reserve school resource officers in schools.

However, a part-time reserve school resource officer shall not be required to meet physical examination requirements or continuing education requirements other than those relating to firearms and use-of-force training.
